title: Differences propagate only downstream; nothing beyond the influence closure exchanges in
summary: Under every law reading a schedule, courses apart at one condition stay alike at every condition not downstream of it. Nothing beyond a formation's influence closure exchanges with what a member depends on.

title: What a response does to an act's difference: rejoining
summary: A difference opens or closes only across steps where the flows exchange differently. On rejoining, what was exchanged makes up the gap exactly. Closing needs a formation outside the part coupling the courses apart; a difference nothing within the responsive reach exchanges with stays. Examples: Replenishing closes, Loop ends support. Open: laws off own courses, many conditions at once.

summary: The theory counts generation and degeneration alike; generation is one part, not a condition on every change; degeneration, ending and mixed change are not renamed generation.

title: Attraction is not returning
summary: A configuration is drawn into an absorbing region iff it does not return; drawn never comes back; reachable set at n is absorbing and draws every lost possibility; finitely, attraction is merging; open worlds separate them; under branching necessarily drawn iff not returning (Transit, OneWay witnesses).

title: T1. Persistence certifies the joint draw
summary: Whatever persists through many renewal cycles of a needed condition has had the joint draw, not its own draw, kept within the margin. The margin belongs to the regime. Under a standing draw, the point of no return lies more than the draw above the need. Proved in the model: joint excess ends the condition, the whole ends with its parts, others outrunning ends it, own draw is not joint draw, a family kept taking from is fed from beyond, and the coupled and web thresholds (RM6-RM10).
note: The thesis part (that actual conditions meet the premises) is supported in the lab and untested in the field.

title: T1 evidence: margin tests in yeast, a simulated commons and fisheries
summary: Passed: MQ2 on real yeast held out (93-100% against a 68-81% null); MQ1 in a simulated Allee yeast (22/22, 12/12); CG1 joint-excess law in about 9.8M windows. Failed: MQ1 D2 (instrument floor); MQ2 C1 (salt shock); MQ3 F3 in fish stocks; MQ6 A1, A2 and T2 (breaks earlier than the constant-regime curves said). No field test with the need measured in advance. Sharpened from own draw to joint draw.

title: T2. State of a renewable condition under a draw: level, recent giving, one lag
summary: Conjectured: three numbers are the state, and no fourth variable removes a tenth of the residual variance. The regime's step and the frozen rest are the two ends of this state. Proved parts: rests over every adjustment (RM2), coming to rest (RM3), the threshold as a curve in the plane of level and recent giving (RM4), any amounts with real convergence in the periphery (RM5), and the coupled step bringing in the partner's level (RM6). Neighbours are delay-difference models (Deriso, Schnute).

title: T2 evidence: MQ4, MQ5, MQ6, MQ7 on fish stocks and yeast
summary: MQ4 on 76 stocks: the pair of level and recent giving is not the whole state (0.12 above the 0.10 bound, failed). MQ5 on 69 stocks: with the lag nothing more is needed (passed), but assessment-model series may carry the lag themselves. MQ7 on 21 unread stocks: 0.39 of the predicted sign, but from 5 stocks with a lower bound of 0.00 (failed). MQ6 lab: residuals are uncorrelated at constant dilution. Predicts across domains: yeast under changing dilution, grassland.
note: Contains AI readings labelled D45.

title: T7. A measure read from what it selects outlives its refutation
summary: Proved in the model: a closed capture loop is one law of the share. An unread loss changes nothing it does. It outlives a loss passing every bound and is turned only through what it reads. The first half is the one lumping law shared with identification and selection. That actual metrics are so formed is conjectured, with no frozen test. Neighbours: Goodhart, Campbell, Wakaiki et al., Everitt et al. 2017, Borkar-Varaiya, self-confirming equilibrium, performativity, Arthur.
note: Could sit in knowing or collective; the capture regime belongs with the map's regimes.

title: Dropped as a thesis: the stronger direction hypothesis
summary: The hypothesis that reality generally develops more shared and more responsive renewal forbids nothing measurable as stated. A part can go on while closing what lies beyond (Clearing.loses_beyond), so persistence does not select widening. It stays an open empirical target, not a premise.
source: THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md, T8, line 1339; also §8.1 targets line 1376 and §8.7 line 1435
note: Stated three times in this unit; carry it once.

title: §8.7 balance from the first law and from continuity
summary: Locality: a quantity carried only by participating exchanges balances exactly where no condition produces it. A total conserved without locality does not balance (Teleport). The first law plus the entropy balance give balance exactly where no store generates entropy, and give the exergy balance. On the core, transfers follow from conservation on every family a relation closes (Continuity).

title: §8.7 dissipation against the second law; Landauer floor
summary: Dissipation as stated is stronger than the statistical second law; Passing is a finite, enclosed, lossless world that never rests. Dissipation needs whole-unit irreversibility or an exergy floor (kT ln 2). A destroyed share gives proportional loss. Dissipation in expectation still ends taking from a closed family almost surely. Landauer needs from physics only the step from count to heat.

title: §8.7 the margin measured (MQ1-MQ7 summary)
summary: The frozen-rest accounting is an identity on measured data, so the test lies in the regime margin. In the lab: thresholds are predicted, and Dai 2012 held out (93-100%). MQ6: breaks came earlier than the constant-regime curves said. In 258 RAM stocks the level is not the state; the state is level, recent giving and lag, near the frozen-rest end. The margin ranks risk but does not time it. MQ7 missed its bound. Harms of joint draws do not add.
note: Duplicates the T1 and T2 evidence; keep one copy, at T1/T2.

title: §8.7 place/transition nets meet the premises by their own definitions
summary: In a finite P/T net, balance is the firing rule, dissipation is a strict P-subinvariant and rest is unrefuted. Emptied siphons stay empty and conservative cycles never rest. This is agreement with known theory, not independent support for generality. Which systems are such nets remains open.

title: Arising recurs exactly when ceasing does, in finite decided worlds
summary: On the spine, arising and ceasing, forming and dissolving, and coming to stand and ceasing to stand are one change read three ways. In a finite world with decided activity, arising recurs exactly when ceasing does. A bounded census keeps them together; an unbounded census does not.
note: the row's caveat on Ren's 不overlap吧 question is outdated: generation and degeneration are now read as non-overlapping

title: Eight World premises are independent; continued arising needs openness
summary: Eight premises (including census and bounded transmission) are each failed by a world meeting the other seven. They decide neither enclosure nor openness. Openness is necessary, not sufficient, for arising without end. Rest comes from finitely many standing and active relata at each step with enclosure, not from finiteness alone.

title: Renewal and consumption belong to runs
summary: A formation renews when every condition it draws on keeps supporting its dependents, and consumes when some dependent loses support for good. The two classes are exclusive but not exhaustive. The class belongs to the run, not to the configuration or the formation's own course: in the same process from the same start, one run renews and another consumes. Joint consumption by two formations that each stay within renewal is also covered.

title: Stepwise reading of renewal and grades of return
summary: [AI reading, D10] An event renews stepwise when its step keeps every dependence it takes part in (RenewingAt). On this reading, living means active and not undermining (MetAbove). It differs from the whole-run reading in both directions and costs something: draws carries no amount. Return is graded from kept to never returning, and consumption is exactly some dependence never returning. Further: no return below support, supported repair (periphery), substitution still consumes.

title: Continued generation needs renewal
summary: Arising means inactive before a step and active after it. In a balanced flow, positive uptake at arbitrarily late steps rules out replenishment that stays zero from some step on. Under dissipation generation is not unceasing, while a closed cycle with constant total sustains it. Unceasing arising is strictly stronger than recurring renewal (Tide).

title: No finite part bears taking under dissipation
summary: Under dissipation, a finite family on which taking recurs is not closed from any step on, and an enclosure around it draws in. With finitely many conditions in all, taking does not recur. Without dissipation, a rise can come without a fall (Brood). Further witnesses: Spray and SprayShuttle.

title: Fed from beyond
summary: Under balance and dissipation, a finite family from which taking recurs, enclosed around from some step on, cannot be fed from nothing beyond it. The proof needs natural-number amounts and fails over reals. What is needed is being fed, not a recurring source.

title: Margin of a regime: exact point of no return (RM1, MQ1, MQ2)
summary: Giving is read off what a standing draw H leaves. A level below H+y ends within as many steps as it stood; at H+y and above it holds. The need belongs to the regime and rises with the draw. Lowered giving raises the need strictly. Harms are superadditive, and two draws that are each survivable alone can end the condition together. Time to break is bounded on both sides. MQ1 (simulated yeast) and MQ2 (real yeast, post hoc) are measured tests. This matches harvesting theory (Clark, May) in whole numbers.

title: Regime point under adjusting giving; rest and threshold curve (RM2-RM4)
summary: When giving adjusts to the level and the recent giving, its rests at or above the draw are exactly the regime's. Giving carried over from before can carry a condition across the point in either direction. Runs within a band come to rest within 3hi+3 steps, and settling needs no omniscience (LastChange.still_within). Overcompensation cycles. The point of no return becomes a least-level curve that does not rise with recent giving, found by finite search. Without monotonicity there is no threshold (Notch).

title: Regime in any ordered amounts and over the reals (RM5)
summary: In any linearly ordered amounts with the draw taken first, a rising adjustment keeps the order of states, and runs have a fixed shape; rests are characterized. In the periphery over the non-negative reals (Mathlib, RegimeReals), runs converge and the fates are down-closed. Whole numbers add finite-time rest and a fate decided at a fixed step; relaxation over the reals converges and never rests.
note: periphery part uses Mathlib axioms

title: Coupled regimes and coupled webs: cascades and thresholds (RM6-RM10)
summary: When giving reads another condition, the point of no return is not the condition's own. Mutual support keeps order and gives least-level thresholds that do not rise with the partner's level. Ends cascade downstream along dependence chains, and rings end together. Inhibition breaks order, and a relay cycles beyond a band. On finite webs, rest is reached within count×band; beyond a band, a bound B on the run gives decision by finite check. These extend to webs with recent giving.
note: RM6-RM10 should be presented as one web law with the pair and regime as cases

title: One law of exact thresholds (UM)
summary: Wherever a fate is down-closed in the level and read off an exact check, the least level at which the check fails is the point of no return. Where one fate implies another, the implied fate's point is no lower. This is the master law that every threshold above instantiates.
note: master law; should lead the regimes chapter rather than trail it

title: A rising take exhausts and ends the seeker
summary: Taking more than now rises by n in n steps. Against a bounded giving, the seeker takes everything after B+1 steps and, under balance, is not active through a bounded window, so it ends. Where renewal is gated, it exhausts the condition for renewers too. A taker that takes everything without its take rising continues.

title: Feeding closure: consumption ends with its feeders
summary: The feeding closure is the least region closed under feeding, and nothing beyond it gives to what a member requires. Under balance, taking from a condition that nothing supported gives to lasts at most its starting level. Overshoot and Clearing (the dweller lies beyond) are the witnesses.

title: Carrying across steps through stores
summary: Earlier giving reaches a later need through a condition that stands throughout; storage can make the closure strict. The exact condition for meeting a need is m + taken ≤ level + given. Withholding both of two redundant feeders can leave no path. Not derived: actual retention, and how a center represents the closure. Reading [D17, D20]: situational awareness is the gap between reach and what couples in.

title: Carried amount, orders as sums over routes, finite order iff no loop
summary: Every gap is at most the carried amount, which is attained and positive along a route of positive strengths. Order j is exact where no loop lies upstream, and a cut loses exactly the next order for every schedule. Orders are route sums in the manner of Dyson and Neumann series (a structural match, not a physical one). The carried amount is polynomial exactly when there is no loop.

title: Loops form by closing; thresholds; observation is a route
summary: A loop forms at the step a coupling closes a chain, and is not foreseeable from prior amounts. Loops lie within what a law reads. Under a law that reads a stock below a threshold, nothing changes up to the break, where the loop forms. A difference reaches a formation only downstream, and observing is the end of such a route.

title: Runaway needs frequent returns; settling ⇔ RecursOrStops ⇔ LPO
summary: Each return at least doubles the carried amount, and frequent returns outgrow every polynomial. A sparse self-loop stays polynomial, so a loop need not run away. The rate counts coupling steps. That every schedule settles is exactly RecursOrStops, which gives LPO.

title: Saturation: a coupling worn to zero (SAT1)
summary: Strengths read off what has passed through a coupling. Once A has passed and strength is zero, the coupling stops and a finite order is exact. With a non-rising response, it stops exactly where the response reaches zero; floored at one, it recurs and leaves every finite order inexact. Passages of 老子 and 韩非 are read onto this [D45].

title: Strength vs factor around a cycle
summary: A strength is given per unit read, and a factor is what a return map multiplies by; for a self-loop the factor is 1+M. One turn around a cycle carries the product of strengths times the amount, plus what the intermediate conditions held. On a ring, 1 + product is a strict lower bound, not the factor. Open: closed-form turns and the spectral radius.

title: More-than-now needs an open world; above-all never rests for two; share rises
summary: 'More than now' needs an open world, and 'above all others' is met by at most one seeker (by definition). Where what stands runs down, rises stop by exhaustion. Where carriers of a target leave more offspring, their share rises (averaging).

title: Runaway: distance to the break does not couple in
summary: Before the break, for every horizon, a world with raised stock is alike through the couplings and lasts longer. A threshold-only policy never uses the larger stock, or uses it only after losing support. Coupling by level passes it at once. The hypothesis excludes early-warning cases (Scheffer 2009).

title: Learning within capture; fulfillment test narrowed to diagnostic
summary: A harmful arrangement can contain genuine learning that maintains a meta-attracting organization. Testing whether ends can change does not certify direction: an organization can help, end its project and still extend control through new dependencies. Revised question: how do the living relations an activity actually forms enter its ends, selection and ending?

title: OPENING: no self can stay closed; lasting proves the joint draw
summary: Whatever is closed and listed comes to rest, and no general method tells when. Whatever keeps taking cannot go on unfed from beyond. Parts that each draw within what is renewed can together exceed it. Lasting proves the joint draw, and one's own restraint proves nothing. A part can go on while it closes others' world.

title: Basin vs viability vs recoverability; prefix renewal condition
summary: An attractor basin, a viability region and a recoverable state are different things. Rule revision and its resources belong in the state. Necessary accounting condition: C0 plus the integral of (R minus L) stays at or above Cmin at every t. Eventual gains cannot pay an earlier irrecoverable loss, and supports keep separate units. This reuses the existing prefix renewal condition and is not a new theorem.
note: Duplicate of the prefix renewal condition (history/THEORY.md §4) and the exact discrete version, equation (14) in MARKET-DYNAMICS-MATH.

title: Enshittification as an institutional form of degeneration
summary: Relations, capacities and dependences formed in shared activity are turned into control that limits later shared creation and correction. Degeneration can occur within refined optimization and commercial growth. Reddit/Apollo (growth with path loss) and the D&D licence (withdrawal after feedback) are entrances, not discoveries. Interface: once consequences are known, how do they gain force over decisions and later rules?
note: The coexistence of growth and loss is explicitly not a new result. The later interface question is the live part.

title: Profit, externalities and reproduced rules
summary: Profit optimization can ignore externalities. The research question is whether cost-shifting advantage enters admission, evaluation and revision rights and reproduces the conditions that favour it. 'External' is relative to the accounting scope; the affected remain in the same process. Rent transfer, externality and erosion of conditions are to be distinguished.
note: Nondual reading of externality, relative to an accounting boundary. Withdraws the weaker 'growth coexists with loss' target.

title: Degenerative meta-attractor boundary: the margin M
summary: Law candidate: erosion of shared conditions gains selective advantage and rebuilds its own selection. Exact boundary in the market model, with M = α(1−θ) − βλθ: next-step protection of the threshold iff M ≥ 0 (M ≥ ε under error); a low-selection certificate exists iff M < 0, with an all-time invariant projection. A benign region coexists at negative margin. 19 Lean theorems.
note: Lean in experiments/market-generativity/formal (boundary-verification.json), not on the spine or Grammar. Separates ethical, mechanism and region boundaries.

title: Four transition routes
summary: A parameter change removes a region's retention condition; a shock moves the state into another retainable region; failure of funds, authority or support stops the correction law being executed; or change is too fast for correction to finish. Region existence change, state departure and strict bifurcation are not one 'phase transition'. Each route can also run toward recovery.

title: Two local attractors and actual support failure
summary: On the β path, equilibria are classified: maintenance end H=(1,1,0), depletion end L_β, and interior S_β for β ≥ 5/12. At β=1/2 both ends attract geometrically and the interior escapes in finite time (38 Lean theorems). With support coupled back in, the low-end neighbourhood exhausts essential support and stops even with correction paid. An attracting organization can erode what it depends on.
note: Lean in attraction-verification.json. Zero share cannot regenerate: a representational limit, not proved irreversibility.

title: Supported finite transition (β set to 0)
summary: For every rational physical state with x > 0, a finite β=0 stage reaches the protected box x ≥ 3/4, q ≥ 1/2, w ≤ 1/4 in finite N, then hands over to the β=1/2 certificate. Sufficient reserve: C0 ≥ K_N = (15+10κ)(10/9)^N − 10(1+κ). Boundaries: x=0 needs entry; no uniform duration; immediate support failure at (1/100, 1/3, 1, 5). 27 Lean theorems.
note: Interim support cannot be paid with future improvement.

title: Partial correction threshold β ≤ 5/12 and fragility to error
summary: In the family 0 ≤ β ≤ 3/4 with zero error, every physical positive-maintenance state enters protection in finite time iff β ≤ 5/12, including equality: partial correction suffices. Recovery at the critical point comes from the retained share x_n ≥ x0/2 lowering influence. Any small persistent error e admits a never-protected equilibrium (32e/5, 3/8, 1−32e/5). 26 Lean theorems.
source: MARKETS-AND-GENERATIVE-REGIMES.md, 'Partial correction, critical feedback and error'
note: Entry is reconstructed from formation results. A free share increment is not allowed.

title: Finite-support obstruction: direction is not timely recovery
summary: For every finite C0 ≥ 5 and integer N > C0 − 5, states with 0 < x0 ≤ (2/3)^N/6 fail by step N under every time-varying β/error sequence and nonnegative stock shock. The projected run may recover while the full guarded history ends first. The same stock sustains a high-maintenance state. A meta-attractor tendency needs an executable supporting history. 17 Lean theorems.
note: 'none' means the market organization ends, not reality. Explains generation, maintenance and disappearance in one history without an ethical premise, under explicit substantive laws.

title: Proposition 2 and the closed capture loop
summary: The fund pays before this round's levy arrives (identity 6). Influence w' = (1−μ)w + μλ(1−x). Accountability q' = clip[(1 − αu − βw)q + αu − e]: selection, influence and exposure form a closed loop of endogenous rule erosion and repair. Proposition 2: with B ≥ k and τ ≥ k, correction is paid every round. If B < k, no later receipt pays the current bill.
source: MARKET-DYNAMICS-MATH.md, 'Paid correction and endogenous rule erosion'
note: Formal capture-through-the-rule mechanism. The legal target and recipe stay fixed; no deliberation invents institutions.

title: Theorem 3: robust invariant region K (sharp for the rectangle)
summary: Under conditions (11) (fund, influence bound, α(1 − q̲) ≥ βw̄q̲ + ε, support inequalities per j), every step from K under every admitted disturbance stays in K. The whole infinite history meets all floors, and the renewing share is nondecreasing. The face conditions are sharp for this rectangular certificate, not necessary for every viable trajectory.
source: MARKET-DYNAMICS-MATH.md, 'A robust invariant region'; separate supports eq. (9)
note: Generative target is componentwise: every support above its floor.

title: Theorem 4: zero-disturbance attraction
summary: From K with no disturbance, states converge to x=1, w=0, q=1, C_j = (r_j − h_j)/δ_j, and B goes to the cap (τ > k) or stays at its inherited value (τ = k), giving a set of equilibria. K is a certified subset of the basin. Real-valued proof via a stable-recursion lemma; Lean does not prove the real limits.

title: Theorem 5: recovery from outside, and the exact prefix floor condition
summary: A sufficient one-step entry condition (13) takes an external starting box into K: genuine recovery from outside the invariant region. Exact discrete prefix condition (14): a positive floor holds through H iff C0 is at least the maximum over t of a_j^(−t)[L_j − Σ a_j^(t−1−s) b_s]. Clipping cannot rescue a crossed positive floor.
note: Exact form of the prefix renewal condition cited in the governance chapter.

title: Theorem 6: destructive region under the same laws
summary: With correction paid every round, the region x ≤ x_D, q ≤ q_D < θ, w ≥ w_D (with α(1 − q_D) ≤ βw_D q_D) is invariant until failure. x decays geometrically and essential supports cross their floors in finite time. Continuously affordable correction can still lose to accumulated influence. Failure is conditional, not inevitable.
source: MARKET-DYNAMICS-MATH.md, 'A destructive region under the same laws'

title: Fully specified rational instance
summary: P=10, τ=k=1, c=2, f=4, ℓ=1/2, η=1/5, α=1/4, β=1/2, μ=1/4, λ=1, r=2, d=1, δ=1/10, L=5; θ = 3/8. Protected box x ≥ 3/4, q ≥ 1/2, w ≤ 1/4 is invariant for e ≤ 1/20, v ≤ 1/2, with C* = 20. A starting collar enters it, and a reversal from (4/5, 7/20, 1/20, 1, 5) reaches the box in one step. Destructive region x ≤ 1/10 fails by C_t ≤ (C0+7)0.9^t − 7.
note: Base instance reused by the β-path results in MARKETS-AND-GENERATIVE-REGIMES.
